title: PM E-DRIVE
summary: Launched in October 2024 to speed up EV adoption, public charging and local manufacturing. Reported outlay is ₹10,900 crore; the end date was extended to March 2028.
benefits: Demand incentives for e-3W, e-buses, e-trucks and e-ambulances continue; the e-2W incentive was phased down and extended only to 31 Jul 2026, so check the current status with the Ministry of Heavy Industries.
₹2,000 crore for public charging: about 72,300 stations targeted (some 2026 reports cite ~88,500), with 80% subsidy on upstream grid works and 100% on government premises.
A National Unified Hub is planned for charger discovery, booking and digital payments.
Linked to a Phased Manufacturing Programme to raise local content.

title: Public charging guidelines
summary: Rules that make it easy to set up chargers and plan networks so drivers are never far from a plug.
benefits: Charging is a de-licensed activity: anyone can set up a public charging station.
Home and office charging is explicitly allowed.
Planning norms call for at least one station in a 3 km × 3 km city grid and one every 25 km on both sides of highways.

title: Concessional GST
summary: EVs and EV chargers attract a 5% GST, far below the 18–40% slabs that apply to most petrol and diesel cars.
benefits: Lower purchase price at the showroom.
Makes charger hardware cheaper for operators.

title: Scheme for electric passenger car manufacturing (SPMEPCI)
summary: Lets approved manufacturers import a limited number of premium completely built-up e-cars at a 15% duty if they commit to build in India.
benefits: Cars must have a CIF value of at least US$35,000.
Applicants commit at least ₹4,150 crore of investment and 25% local value addition by year 3, rising to 50% by year 5.
Up to 8,000 cars a year can be imported at the reduced duty.

title: Production-linked incentive (PLI) schemes
summary: Two PLI programmes reward domestic manufacturing: the Auto and auto components scheme and the Advanced Chemistry Cell (battery) scheme.
benefits: Auto PLI: ₹25,938 crore for advanced automotive technology including EVs.
ACC battery PLI: about ₹18,100 crore to build 50 GWh of cell manufacturing in India.

title: State EV policies
summary: Most states add their own benefits on top of central support. Delhi, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Telangana and others have published EV policies.
benefits: Road tax and registration-fee waivers are common.
Some states add purchase incentives and charger subsidies.
Check your state transport department for current rules.

title: Green plates and permit exemption
summary: Battery-operated vehicles get green number plates and are exempt from transport permit requirements (MoRTH, 2018).
benefits: Easier registration for commercial EVs.
Makes EVs easy to identify for local incentives like parking or toll benefits.

title: PM e-Bus Sewa
summary: A public-private partnership scheme to put around 10,000 electric buses on city routes in about 169 cities, backed by roughly ₹57,600 crore.
benefits: Cuts urban air and noise pollution.
Creates demand that helps charging networks scale.

title: FAME I and II (earlier schemes)
summary: India's first large EV demand-incentive programmes, which ran from 2015 and 2019. A short interim scheme (EMPS) followed before PM E-DRIVE began in October 2024.
benefits: Seeded the first wave of e-2W, e-3W and e-bus adoption.
Introduced local-content conditions that PM E-DRIVE builds on.
